Hollow stags are wary woodland animals whose calls carry unexpectedly through old timber. None is automatically a demon, an alchemical cure or a reliable omen. Their distribution, rarity and practical effects require local authoring before they become gameplay facts.

Danger often comes from familiar systems under strain: a neglected shaft, a flooded store, contaminated water, a predator displaced by logging or a road made unsafe by people protecting an illicit trade. Spectacular threats can exist, but a living continent should not need a new ancient evil to explain every broken promise.

sections.title: Institutions between the nations
paragraphs: The Rangers of Larius are the best-known institution able to move among several states without being identical to any one of them. Their independence is always negotiated. Permission to cross a border, carry arms, investigate a complaint or transport a prisoner must come from the circumstances and the relevant authority, rather than from the fame of their leader.

The League of Safe Roads is an association of carriers, hostel keepers, merchants and communities interested in keeping routes usable. It funds repairs and reports hazards, but its priorities favour roads its members use. A neglected village can reasonably ask why the league’s language of universal safety stops at a profitable junction.

The Witness Houses preserve copies of agreements and testimony in several jurisdictions. They sell dependable custody and comparison of documents. Their great virtue is the possibility that a powerful patron cannot destroy every copy. Their weakness is the temptation to treat access to an archive as a private service when its contents govern public lives.

The Lantern houses, Hearth Leagues, Last Door fellowship and local assemblies create further connections across borders. A crisis may be addressed through them when formal diplomacy is too slow. Their members still have interests, prejudices and legal limits. Cooperation is an accomplishment, not a universal power granted by good intentions.

The central institutional question for Kieran is whether the Rangers will become something able to survive his judgement. A company that does good only because one exceptional man always knows what to do has a fragile future. A company with accountable practices may sometimes reach a decision he dislikes.

sections.title: The present tensions — The expedition charter
paragraphs: Negotiation of the westward fleet’s charter is a central continental story. Who may speak for the expedition? What happens when a sponsor’s interests differ from an agreement made abroad? Can a ranger refuse an order that a financier believes was already purchased? Does a place found by Larius automatically become something Larius may claim?

Akaria and Southern Estru are connected to the offer in Kieran’s record. Other interests may seek participation, information, guarantees or the opportunity to stop a competitor. The destination remains unspecified. TalmahKah, Aldain, Azaloth, Falkion and Bendara are not silently assigned as targets or assumed to be unknown to their own inhabitants.

sections.title: The present tensions — The names absent from the peace
paragraphs: A proposed dispute concerns surviving copies of the settlement of 400 A.A. Different versions appear to account differently for some displaced communities. The premise creates an investigation, not proof that every old treaty was forged. Mistake, damaged records, selective copying and deliberate exclusion are all possibilities to establish through later authoring or play.

Kieran’s memories matter, but recollection is not an all-purpose answer. A person may remember the day of a surrender and still not know what a minister negotiated elsewhere. A respected witness can have been misled.

sections.title: The present tensions — The cost of the new workshops
paragraphs: Trade and manufacture create prosperity while shifting risk. An unsafe factory, an exploitative supply contract or a town dependent on one purchaser can bring the states’ public promises into conflict. This story can involve sincere reformers and responsible employers alongside cynical ones. It should not require every inventor to be reckless or every worker to agree on the remedy.

sections.title: The present tensions — A republic’s living royal descendant
paragraphs: Kieran’s lineage becomes newly useful to people who want to legitimize political change. A royalist can seek restoration, a republican can seek his endorsement and an outside power can threaten to recognize a claim he has never made. His refusal to be a king does not automatically stop others from spending political capital on the possibility.

sections.title: The present tensions — Who inherits the Rangers?
paragraphs: The company’s founding refugees included several peoples. Its present membership is recorded as elven only. Descendants of its mortal founders can honour that history while asking why a story about common rescue now authorizes exclusion. Existing Rangers may fear losing the practices that hold the company together. Kieran must face the question without a predetermined answer to the company’s membership question.

sections.title: The present tensions — The demand that nobody die
paragraphs: Continuance patrons offer support for healing research and then ask what access that support has bought. The Last Door fellowship presses for accountable practice. Bereaved families ask for help that neither institution can promise. Kieran’s reputation makes silence a public statement, but speaking honestly may disappoint people who need hope more urgently than an explanation.

These tensions have no scheduled victories, forced betrayals or guaranteed wars. Each can develop through the independent priorities of its people. Kieran is central because he is connected to the questions, not because nothing can happen until he arrives.

sections.title: Places worth knowing
paragraphs: These places anchor the continent’s political and personal histories. Their exact coordinates and measured routes remain to be developed.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Karkaria
paragraphs: The imperial underground capital should feel like a city made through successive decisions rather than excavated in one miraculous act. Old routes, prestigious halls and later works coexist. A new vent may provoke a more consequential argument than a court ceremony. The memorial tablets include the names of people who died maintaining the city, and arguments about which names were left out. Karwathis is the superseded map label for this capital; the current name is Karkaria.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Forlathis
paragraphs: Kieran’s birthplace lives with visitors who want to find the beginning of his legend. Its inhabitants have ordinary reasons to care about rent, work and local decisions. A proposed public commemoration of his parents has become a disagreement about which version of the republican founding the town will endorse. Kieran can be invited to speak without being entitled to settle it.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Tethris and Evalia
paragraphs: The former and present capitals carry different kinds of prestige. Tethris preserves the social memory of the monarchy and the inconvenience of being treated as a place whose importance ended. Evalia houses republican ceremony, argument and the work of governing. Families, artists and scholars move between them. Old royal associations do not make every resident of Tethris a restorationist; residence in the republican capital does not prove a commitment to equal representation.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Bay Watch
paragraphs: The capital of Sadion gives the kingdom’s protective claims a visible stage: petitions, naval business, provisioning, court display and people waiting for an answer. The setting gives its waterfront a strong culture of collective practical knowledge. A clerk may know which cargo can wait; a dock worker may know why it cannot. When the two trust one another, a crisis can be solved before anyone makes a speech.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Griffin
paragraphs: Griffin should contain the possibility of a life that Daniel’s childhood did not offer him. Crowded lodging houses, workshops, small traders, neighbourhood kitchens and recruiting offices make it a place of opportunity and extraction. A successful former orphan can become a benefactor, a convenient public example or a person reminded that he has not repaired the conditions from which he escaped.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Vlaris
paragraphs: Vlaris is a city of arrivals with a long memory of departures. Its meaning to Kieran includes the anonymous life he tried to make after the war. Workshops and households retain private recollections that do not resemble official biography. The public revelation of an old friendship could be moving for one participant and intrusive for the other.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Cthulis
paragraphs: Cthulis carries the memory of siege, capture and resistance. The expanded city is neither permanently ruined nor perfectly restored. Its newer work stands over older foundations; families differ over which traces should remain visible. Someone whose home is inconveniently protected as a war memorial may have an understandable view of commemorative enthusiasm.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Estru City
paragraphs: The map gives Estru City prominent standing. The setting presents it as a place where the meaning of independence is argued through contracts, employment and the control of civic spaces. Public meals and foreign warehouses belong to the same streets. The city’s exact present constitutional rank remains unselected; the wider Estrusian political settlement remains to be developed.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Castle LuCain
paragraphs: The castle anchors the expedition thread without requiring a new war to begin at its gates. It is a useful setting for negotiations among sponsors, hired specialists, carriers, religious witnesses and people seeking passage. Its authority over the expedition must be established by agreement, not inferred from the fact that everyone has gathered there. The castle’s jurisdiction remains among the geography questions to resolve.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Ikarion
paragraphs: Ikarion, spelled Ikrarion in older accounts, passed to Everwood during the war. Its households carry different memories of the same settlement: a claim recognized, a home retained under another flag, or a voice excluded from the agreement. It offers a setting for arguments about title, inherited residence and who was entitled to negotiate for the people who remained.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Dole’s March, Fort Corinth and SunWatch
paragraphs: These map names offer three local perspectives beyond the capitals. Dole’s March can develop the encounter between military memory and the people supplying it. Fort Corinth can place public safety against the priorities of those living near a guarded route. SunWatch can explore the meeting of Akarian surface life and traditions formed underground. These are suggested local emphases, not newly enacted garrison orders or confirmed administrative arrangements.

sections.title: Places worth knowing — Nucarius’ Tower
paragraphs: Nucarius’ Tower is associated with observation, copied records and the comparison of what different witnesses believe they saw. Scholars of weather and the sky work alongside keepers of older testimony. Their instruments and disagreements offer knowledge with limits, rather than an omniscient view of the continent. Its most useful secret may be a neglected piece of ordinary evidence.

sections.title: New recurring people
paragraphs: The following people belong to the setting’s supporting cast. Their work, loyalties and disagreements continue beyond Kieran’s presence. Their first scenes remain open to the particular campaign or story.

Lethra Senn is an Evalian archivist who admires the republic enough to be angered by its evasions. She wants important agreements made publicly intelligible. Kieran’s memory interests her, but she refuses to cite his reputation as a substitute for corroboration. She can become a trusted collaborator precisely because she is prepared to discover that he is mistaken.

Dorrun Valehammer is an Akarian works inspector committed to making industrial expansion defensible to the people bearing its risks. He respects Cathius without assuming that imperial goodwill prevents negligence. A Hearth League may regard him as an ally on one project and a defender of the owners on another. He wants standards that survive a change of patron.

Rovan Kest is a Sadire former quartermaster who carries petitions from soldiers’ households. He knows the temptation to redirect an inadequate supply and defend the decision afterward. His loyalty to the kingdom is real. So is his willingness to embarrass its officers when they prefer ceremonial gratitude to the delivery of promised help.

Neris Tal is a Kyrinian navigator and negotiator associated with an Open Horizon house. She wants an expedition charter that can survive contact with people whose consent its sponsors have not yet sought. She will respect Kieran’s experience and still ask when he last accepted terms set by somebody less famous than himself.

Vessa Morn organizes a Shared Table in Southern Estru and earns her living keeping accounts for households that cannot afford mistakes. She refuses to choose between feeding people now and questioning the arrangement that keeps them dependent. Foreign patrons find her useful until she applies the same scrutiny to their generosity as to their contracts.

Sera Vael is an elven Ranger who manages practical company affairs: supplies, apprenticeships, care and the memory of promises. She believes the company needs procedures that can constrain its founder. Her loyalty is tested when admirers of Kieran treat every request for accountability as an insult to his sacrifices.

Taren Ash is a healer associated with the Last Door fellowship. He supports careful restoration research while insisting that a successful outcome does not prove a justified method. He can defend Kieran against a false accusation and challenge him over a real failure in the same conversation. His disagreement is most effective when it comes from shared concern rather than fear of all magic.

Each person needs relationships, resources and limits beyond the central character. Vessa has a community to answer to; Dorrun has colleagues and cases; Neris has obligations to people who may never meet a Ranger. They should continue to have reasons to act when Kieran is elsewhere.

sections.title: Kieran and The Price of Peace
paragraphs: The separate Kieran dossier develops his interior life, public roles, relationships, failings, exceptional longevity and present arc. The organizing idea is that the continent’s main character can matter enormously without being the continent’s owner.

The Price of Peace is the setting’s central continuing arc. It connects the western charter, the treatment of old testimony, the Rangers’ membership and succession, industrial change and the politics of restoration. These are several problems with their own causes, not a hidden single conspiracy that explains every disagreement.

Kieran’s old strategy is to carry the danger himself, hold the painful truth until the right moment and use personal trust to bridge institutions that do not trust one another. That strategy has saved people. It has also left too many arrangements dependent on one person’s judgement.

The question is whether he can distribute responsibility without abandoning care. Other people must be allowed to know enough to choose, to disagree without losing his protection, and to build institutions he cannot personally supervise forever. A satisfying story can make him less indispensable while making his contribution more lasting.

This arc needs no predetermined ending. He might learn to release authority, become more controlling under pressure, suffer a failure, find an unexpected partner or lose the chance to resolve a question himself. The world remains able to continue. Its people inherit what he actually did rather than what a legend promised he would do.

sections.title: Canon and further development
paragraphs: This expanded worldbook and the Kieran dossier establish the current Larius setting, as adopted by the creator in KIRA-U06. The earlier documents remain an archive of the world’s development and have no authority to overrule this edition. The creator’s national inspirations, caste relationships, Desert and Ice Elven details and separate continental shelves remain foundations of the setting.

The reference present is 1342 A.A. The continental war spans 80–400 A.A.; Kieran’s active service accounts for 228 years within it. Independence belongs to 500 A.A. And Estru’s later invasion to 600 A.A. Kieran’s Long Renewal accounts for his exceptional age. Karkaria, Evalia, Ikarion and Daniel Convor are the current names; superseded spellings stay in the archive and map transcription.

The eight religious traditions, developed national cultures, interregional institutions, supporting cast, creatures, Sivren, Keld and Vesh belong to this canon. A possible negotiation, investigation or future personal choice is still a story opening. Its inclusion does not establish a completed event or determine who succeeds.

Religious teachings remain beliefs held by people in the setting. They do not establish a fully known cosmology. Exact constitutions, unassigned caste positions, route distances and numerical magic rules remain further development. Existing campaign events retain their own history; the worldbook supplies no automatic change to a live campaign.

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — The man and the symbol
paragraphs: Kieran was born in Forlathis in 1000 B.A., at the close of the Evalian civil war. His father was the first prime minister of the republic; his mother was the daughter of the dethroned king. At 2342, he has outlived the founding crisis without escaping its meaning.

His snow-white hair, height, quiet manner and white Evalian stallion make him recognizable before anyone hears his name. He carries two steel sabers, an Evalian-wood bow, leather clothing reinforced with mithral and the practical tools of a traveller. He should look like someone who maintains useful things rather than someone who acquires a new sacred weapon each time the story changes direction.

The public sees an ancient ranger, a possible prince, an extraordinary mage and a witness who has survived what states prefer to call settled history. Those identities can be used against one another. Asking for his blessing can be an attempt to purchase legitimacy. Asking him to remember can be a way of demanding that he publicly accuse a friend.

Kieran’s own sense of himself is less grand. He measures a day by whether people who depended on him came home, whether an apprentice learned something useful and whether he can stand by the terms under which he accepted work. He notices the damaged stitching on a cloak before the embroidery on a minister’s robe.

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — What he wants, and what he has yet to learn
paragraphs: His immediate desire is to protect the people in his care without becoming the instrument of another preventable war. His deeper need is to accept that protection cannot mean possession of everyone else’s choices.

He is brave, nurturing and genuinely capable of care, as his actions and relationships show. His experience can nevertheless become a form of control. He may withhold a painful detail because he fears what someone will do with it. He may assign himself a risk that another person was entitled to choose. He can mistake the ability to endure another loss for permission to decide who must be spared it.

His guilt over the scout’s arrow is the centre of this pattern. The failure was real: he did not stop a member of his command from turning a fraught encounter into violence. But guilt becomes misleading when he treats it as an explanation for every decision made by every state afterward. Blaming himself for everything also places him at the centre of everything. Learning to recognize other people’s responsibility is part of learning to respect their agency.
The question that follows him is: “Can I help build something that does not need me to hold it together?” He has led the Rangers for centuries. He has had ample reason to postpone answering.

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — What he wants, and what he has yet to learn — The inheritance he does not stop carrying
paragraphs: Everwood’s confirmed caste order sharpens his position. He is a Plains elf, belonging to one of the numerous groups that Sea elves recognize as equals despite their own sense of magical superiority. His royal maternal lineage and republican paternal lineage give him additional prestige. His exceptional magic lets him enter settings in which a less favoured elf may be praised for useful service and denied comparable standing.

Mountain elves make the problem particularly visible: their strength is valued against Human and Dwarven enemies while weaker magic becomes an excuse to look down on them. Kieran can defend elves fiercely and still have learned assumptions about which elves should lead. His character need not begin as a modern egalitarian untouched by his upbringing. What he notices, excuses, resists or chooses to unlearn belongs to his continuing story.

The Rangers’ mix of elven ancestries can expose those assumptions in practical terms. If a Mountain Ranger is trusted to hold a line, is that same Ranger trusted to help set the company’s policy? Recognizing skill only where it serves an inherited hierarchy can become one of Kieran’s own failures, not merely an offence he identifies in other people.

The Desert Elves complicate any account in which he treats Estru simply as Sadire descendants needing an elven intermediary. They helped form that society themselves. He must learn whom a local assembly has authorized to speak, rather than assuming an elven household will welcome him as its natural representative. Their history is not merely a lesson arranged for his benefit.

The Ice Elves challenge a different assumption: magical distinction does not require recognition by Evalia or by Kieran. Their superior magical inheritance does not rank every individual above him, but it denies his homeland an uncomplicated claim to be the measure of all elven achievement. A proposed story could put his friendship with Cathius alongside an Ice Elven request concerning viable habitat. He can help secure a hearing without owning the settlement, speaking for the community or proving his concern through a spectacular spell.

The existence of other minor peoples adds a wider test. A famous negotiator between the five dominant societies may still overlook people those states do not treat as parties to an agreement. His refugee rescue remains a real achievement. It need not prove that he has already learned to hear every kind of voice.

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — His long life
paragraphs: Kieran is 2342 years old. His exceptional healing knowledge has prolonged his life far beyond the ordinary Plains Elven reference span of about 1000 years. Plains and Flatland are names for the same elven group; its ordinary lifespan is a reference span rather than an inviolable biological maximum.

The practice is called the Long Renewal. It is sustained personal healing and painstaking study of his own changing body, not a resurrection guarantee or a divine exemption from death. Wounds, illness, failed treatment and deliberate violence can still kill him. The precise method, reproducibility and supernatural costs remain undeveloped authoring questions; no new executable ability is granted by this explanation.

Renewing a body does not restore every lost memory, preserve every relationship or make centuries emotionally interchangeable. He can remember an old battlefield’s smell and fail to recall a friend’s laugh. He keeps written recollections partly because his confidence in a memory is not proof that it is complete.

People interpret his survival according to their own needs. A Turning Bough teacher may see an unfinished duty. A Continuance researcher sees evidence worth studying. A royalist may call it a sign that his bloodline must return. Kieran dislikes the last interpretation, but dislike does not prevent it from spreading.

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — The Ranger before the legend
paragraphs: His mother taught him the bow, his father taught him dual swordsmanship and a tutor introduced him to magic. He helped secure the lands that became Kyrinus and later commanded men in the frontier crisis with Akaria. His active service during the continental war spanned 228 years. He later withdrew to Vlaris, living under another name and learning skills that had little to do with public honour. The continental conflict itself lasted from 80 to 400 A.A.; the personal span is not the length of the whole war.

His hundred years of withdrawal were a period of changed work and ordinary relationships. Someone who knew him then may remember a competent leatherworker with an irritating habit of repairing other people’s tools without being asked. They need not have understood his lineage or the extent of his power.

The evacuation during the rebellions of 500 A.A. Brought him back into a different kind of responsibility. The people he helped escape included Karthinians, Estrusians, Akarians, Evalians and Sadire. The early Rangers grew from people who had chosen one another while their states demanded separation.

Their present elven-only membership is therefore not an incidental recruitment rule. It is a contradiction inside the company’s memory. Kieran may have reasons for preserving it; he also has reasons to question whether the institution has remembered its founders honestly. The setting should let that question hurt without assigning him a ready-made answer.

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — Faith, death and the use of power
paragraphs: Kieran respects practices that make people responsible to one another. His personal religious life draws most closely on the Turning Bough, especially its insistence that memory should nourish the living rather than govern them forever. He is not its chosen messiah, high priest or final authority.

He keeps private observances for people he could not save. Publicly reading their names is difficult because listeners often want to turn confession into proof of virtue. He would prefer that the dead be remembered as people rather than as a measure of his suffering.

His relationship with restoration is similarly uncomfortable. His study of resurrection and raising the dead arises partly from compassion and partly from his inability to bear an old failure. He can do good with knowledge acquired for a troubling reason. He can also be tempted to cross a boundary because refusing feels too much like abandoning someone again.

He rejects the proposition that a person restored to life owes obedience to the restorer. He also knows that gratitude can become dependence without anyone stating the bargain aloud. The Last Door fellowship can challenge him precisely where his good intentions are strongest.

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — The people who can reach him
paragraphs: Cathius Akarian is a personal friend. Their friendship lets Kieran see a dwarven ruler as a man who has made choices within an aggressive, insular and often xenophobic imperial society. It also gives both men grounds for uncomfortable exceptions: an Akarian courtier can admire Kieran without respecting elves generally, and Kieran can respect Cathius while understating the costs Akaria imposes on weaker neighbours. Cathius values Kieran’s honesty and sometimes grows impatient with his habit of making a difficult decision sound like a responsibility he must bear alone. Kieran, in turn, sees the danger in an emperor assuming that reforms sensible to him will arrive harmlessly everywhere his goods are sold.

Lord Eric Vornwolf is also a friend. His exact domain remains unassigned in the current setting. He can speak to Kieran outside institutional performance; his wider realm or office remains to be developed. Their private disagreements can be authored once his wider place in the setting is established.

Everwood’s officials need his testimony and worry about his symbolic authority. The more accepting, mercantile society of Kyrinus can respect his wartime courage while exposing the condescension he has learned to disguise as patient advice. The Karthinian Council can reject any suggestion that he remains entitled to supervise its people. Ordinary Rangers know the habits the public legend misses: when he becomes quiet for the wrong reason, when he has not slept and when he is preparing to leave a dangerous task to himself.

He needs relationships in which correction does not become betrayal. Without them, longevity can turn the company of younger people into an endless procession of dependants who are never allowed to become equals.

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — How to write him in a scene
paragraphs: Kieran speaks plainly when someone needs a practical answer. He becomes guarded when asked what a failure meant to him. He asks names and remembers tasks. He gives a nervous person something useful to do instead of making reassurance into a performance.

He is not humourless. His humour is dry, occasionally badly timed and often directed at the difference between a grand description and a familiar inconvenience. When comfortable, he enjoys good work, ordinary meals and the quiet satisfaction of teaching someone a repair that will last.

His defensiveness about insults against elves is an inherited trait worth retaining as a flaw. It can reveal where generosity stops being as even-handed as he believes. A human or dwarf who has earned his respect can challenge that inconsistency without being treated by the narrative as insolent for noticing it.

When angry he tends toward precision. He may become dangerously certain before he becomes loud. When afraid of losing someone he can offer a reasonable-sounding plan whose real purpose is to remove their choice. Neither tendency erases his care; both make it a source of conflict.
Sample dialogue: “You can ask me what I remember. You cannot ask my memory to make the choice for you.”
Sample dialogue: “The contract says who pays us. It does not decide who we are allowed to leave behind.”
Sample dialogue: “If the Rangers cannot tell me I am wrong, I have built a court and called it a company.”

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — His present story
paragraphs: The central arc is called The Price of Peace in this edition. The expedition offer, contested historical records, the Rangers’ future and the politics of restoration all ask versions of the same question: can Kieran help people move beyond the settlements that shaped him without deciding their future on their behalf?

He may support a voyage, expose an injustice, defend a friend, refuse a profitable commission or discover that his first interpretation was wrong. None of those outcomes is scheduled. His centrality comes from the weight of his connections and choices.

Other characters can accomplish things he cannot, challenge his priorities, defeat his plans and carry a story beyond his reach. If he dies, the continent loses a central person and must live with the consequences. It does not become an invalid campaign world.

sections.title: Kieran Pelleas — Canon and authorship
paragraphs: This dossier is adopted setting canon under KIRA-U06. Kieran’s Long Renewal, personal faith, habits, flaws, relationships and central arc are part of the current characterization. The earlier character sheet is a superseded creative archive. Later creator directions can revise this characterization without needing agreement from an older document.
The Price of Peace presents an ongoing conflict with open outcomes. Kieran’s narrative centrality supplies no guaranteed survival, automatic authority or player selection.

records.name: Kira
records.summary: The World of Kira is a homebrew fantasy setting. Its supplied records now cover Larius, TalmahKah, Aldain, Azaloth, Falkion and Bendara, with the most detailed written histories centred on Larius.
records.attribution: World identity and purpose supplied by the user in this conversation; regional identities also occur in the archive directory names.

records.name: Larius
records.summary: The principal recorded region, containing the human, elven and dwarven nations and the Rangers of Larius.
records.scale: Rangers record says continent; no map, coordinates or distances supplied.

estru.historical_context: Sadire settlement preceded the transition to Estru; centuries have passed

records.name: TalmahKah
records.summary: A region represented by a Minecraft reference map with thirty-two named entries and a Word list describing the Lupine.
records.attribution: Regional association comes from the original archive path, not an inferred map.

records.name: Before Ascension / After Ascension
records.summary: The dwarven emergence onto the surface marks the calendar transition. B.A. counts before Ascension; A.A. counts after it. The dwarven history explicitly names 1342 as present day.
records.arithmetic_policy: Ascension is the calendar turning; 1342 A.A. is the reference present. Exact civil months and time conversions remain undeveloped.

records.name: Akarian Empire
records.summary: A dwarven empire centred on Iron Hill and the underground capital Karkaria. Its history describes ten underground cities and five surface cities in 1342 A.A. Cathius Akarian is the recorded emperor.
records.capability_status: Industrial and military superlatives are source descriptions; exact population, production, stock and force totals are unprovided.

creator_confirmed_profile.name: Akaria
confirmed_traits: Heavily armoured cavalry on large Rams intended to smash enemy lines

records.name: Kingdom of Sadion
records.summary: The Sadire human kingdom, with Bay Watch as its recorded capital. Its present king is Erik Vollan, whose son is Alek Vollan. Its institutions include the Legion of Valiance, a navy and a Hunter corps.

creator_confirmed_profile.name: Sadion
military_inspirations: Roman legionary institutions and broad tactics

records.name: Grand Republic of Evalia
records.summary: The elven republic of Everwood. Its history describes city and village representatives meeting four times a year and gives an assembly total of 256. The current prime minister is unnamed.
records.note: Population subtypes are recorded in the Larius list; their current citizenship and political distribution are not enumerated.

creator_confirmed_profile.name: Everwood / Evalia
cultural_inspirations: French-influenced cultural prestige; no accent caricature
confirmed_traits: Elves remain the most magically powerful peoples of Larius
Sub-race-based caste system persists within a republic

sea_elves.attitude_to_plains_and_tree: feel superior but recognize them as equals

mountain_elves.military_value: strength and efficiency fighting Humans and Dwarves
mountain_elves.status: looked down upon for insufficient magical capabilities

magic_and_status.interpretation: Highest recognized Evalian caste and greatest elven magical capability are separate claims; superior Ice Elven magic does not establish their caste rank.

records.name: Kyrinus
records.summary: The Karthinian elven nation, founded as an Evalian colony in 40 A.A. It rebelled in 500 A.A., gained independence after defeat and later renewed trade with Everwood. A non-aggression pact is recorded between the elven nations.
records.institution: Karthinian Council mentioned in Kieran’s biography; composition and current officeholders unknown.

records.name: Estru
records.summary: A pressured, politically divided society shaped by Sadire-descended humans and long-resident Desert Elves. Independent since 500 A.A., it lost its later war against Sadion in 600 A.A.; Southern Estru trades with Akaria.
records.note: The present constitutional relationship between Estru and its southern part is not established; Castle LuCain’s political location is also unprovided.

creator_confirmed_profile.name: Estru
confirmed_traits: Estrusian humans descend from the Sadire; Estru also has a foundational Desert Elven population
Oppressed by larger and more powerful neighbours
Desert Elves were initially unwilling residents in the history associated with Sadire settlement
Centuries of residence and Desert Elven contributions helped form Estru culturally

records.childhood_and_succession: Started public work at 15; styled Revered One at 20; assumed ruling duties after his mother died at 35; crowned after his father died when Cathius was 50.
records.abilities: Two-handed weapons and guns are named expertise; no IRGS ratings selected.

records.resources: The 200,000 gold in the childhood account is a historical claim, not a current balance.

records.abilities: Named mastery labels and spell names remain source descriptions, not selected IRGS ranks or resolved effects.
records.relationships: Friend of Cathius Akarian and Lord Eric Vornwolf; connected to the Evalian republic and Karthinian Council. These relationships confer no automatic mandate.

continuity_issues.title: Kieran’s longevity
continuity_issues.resolution: Kieran is a Plains Elf, also called Flatland Elf, born in 1000 B.A. and aged 2342 in 1342 A.A. His sustained healing practice, the Long Renewal, extends his life beyond the ordinary Plains Elven reference span of about 1000 years. It provides no immunity or guaranteed resurrection.

continuity_issues.title: Duration of the dwarven war
continuity_issues.resolution: The continental dwarven war runs from 80 to 400 A.A., a span of 320 years. The 228-year figure describes Kieran’s active wartime service, not the duration of the whole war. Exact enlistment and withdrawal years are not separately fixed.

continuity_issues.title: The rebellion and separation dates
continuity_issues.resolution: Estru and Kyrinus gain independence in 500 A.A. Estru’s later failed invasion of Sadion belongs to 600 A.A.

continuity_issues.title: Estru and Southern Estru
continuity_issues.question: What are Estru’s current political divisions, rulers and relationship with Akaria?

continuity_issues.title: Map and disputed colonial geography
continuity_issues.question: What are the relative positions of the six shelves, which dates do the maps represent, and what world-distance scale should apply?

continuity_issues.title: Spelling and identity variants
continuity_issues.resolution: Use Akarian for Akaria’s dwarves; Evalian for Everwood’s political identity; Sadire for Sadion’s human people; Estrusian for Estru’s civic identity, including its human and Desert Elven populations; Karthinian for Kyrinus’s civic elven society; Daniel Convor for Dan/Fox. Plains and Flatland denote the same elven group; Tree and Forest denote the same elven group. Karthi remains a distinct historical name.

continuity_issues.title: Magic and technology rules
continuity_issues.question: Which magical capabilities and limitations define Kira, and how widely available are guns and enchanted items?

continuity_issues.title: Early Sadion chronology
continuity_issues.resolution: The early sequence is Sadire migration and settlement, Grad’s consolidation and founding of the Legion, followed by San’s institutional development. Sadion is unified by the opening of trade with the elves in 1998 B.A. The ambiguous archival phrase After 2000 supplies no separate date or 2000-year interval.

continuity_issues.title: World baseline and authored starting snapshots
continuity_issues.question: Which source material belongs to the chosen 1342 world baseline, and which earlier eras should receive separate developed snapshots?

continuity_issues.question: Was TalmahKah the intended western destination, and what happened on that expedition?

continuity_issues.title: Map capitals and written place names
continuity_issues.resolution: Karkaria is Akaria’s underground capital; Karwathis is its superseded map label. Evalia names the republican capital as well as the republic; Evalian on the map is a label variant. Ikarion is the current place name; Ikrarion is an older spelling for the same place.
